assertions_contracts.best_practice: Unchanged in 0.16: asserts are for established invariants, comptime for provable properties, and unreachable remains a correctness claim whose violation is illegal behaviour in unsafe modes. The guide's insistence on testing rejection in ReleaseFast matches upstream's own warning that safety checks are mode-dependent.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Guide's citations [Z1]/[Z2] are the current 0.16.0 language reference and release notes; no later release has altered these semantics (no 0.16.x patch release exists as of this audit).
assertions_contracts.guide_position: std.debug.assert for internal invariants (one per assert), comptime checks for static properties, unreachable never as a fallback or for external failure.

bounded_work.best_practice: No upstream equivalent policy exists - bounding is an application discipline in Zig, and 0.16's allocator-explicit, capacity-explicit container redesign (unmanaged containers, AssumeCapacity variants) makes the guide's style easier, not obsolete.
bounded_work.evidence: The 0.16 release's unmanaged-container migration, which the guide already reflects in its container section, is the current upstream direction.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named *_max constants for loops, allocations, retries, queues, nesting and captured output; explicit stacks instead of unbounded recursion; retries idempotent with a shared deadline.

concurrency.best_practice: 0.16's model is exactly what the guide describes: I/O is an interface parameter (the 'juicy main' pattern), with Threaded/Evented backends, futures/groups and cancellation as an error path; language-level async from pre-0.15 examples is gone.
concurrency.evidence: The 0.16.0 release notes are the guide's own cited source for the Io migration; multiple independent 0.16 migration records confirm std.Io Threaded/futures/groups as the shipped design and std.fs-era snippets as obsolete.
concurrency.guide_position: Pass the Io dependency explicitly (0.16 interface-based I/O), bound group size, cancel and await owned work before freeing its data, cancellation is a real error path, thread-safe allocator does not imply thread-safe objects.

error_handling.best_practice: Error unions remain Zig's sole error mechanism in 0.16 and the documented idiom is unchanged: specific error sets, try to propagate, catch for a stated recovery, defer/errdefer for cleanup. 0.16 did not add exceptions, result types or a generic anyerror recommendation.
error_handling.evidence: The 0.16.0 documentation set the guide cites is still the current stable documentation; the release notes' breaking changes concern I/O, containers and process APIs, not error-union semantics.
error_handling.guide_position: Documented error unions on fallible paths, no anyerror on public surfaces, try propagates, catch only for a specific recovery, defer/errdefer never double-free, no catch unreachable on external failure, OOM or config.

formatting.best_practice: zig fmt is the official formatter shipped with the compiler and remains the single sanctioned style; upstream style is likewise 4-space indentation produced by the formatter, not by hand.
formatting.evidence: The guide's formatter claim matches the toolchain it pins; ZLS releases track the same version line and delegate formatting to the same canonical style.
formatting.guide_position: zig fmt owns formatting (~100-col readable lines, ~70-line functions as review aids), zig fmt --check in CI, never fight its output.

memory_ownership.best_practice: 0.16 strengthens the guide's position: containers are unmanaged by default (allocator passed per operation), GeneralPurposeAllocator was renamed DebugAllocator in the 0.15/0.16 line, and the std.Io redesign makes capability-passing the universal pattern. Caller-buffer/fixed-capacity first, explicit allocator second, remains idiomatic upstream style.
memory_ownership.evidence: 0.16 release-note summaries and migration records list unmanaged std.ArrayList as default, allocator arguments on mutating methods, and renamed/removed helpers (GeneralPurposeAllocator -> DebugAllocator, fixedBufferStream -> Io.Writer.fixed) - all consistent with, and already reflected in, the guide.
memory_ownership.guide_position: Allocators are parameters, never globals; caller buffers/fixed capacity preferred; defer/errdefer discipline with a documented freeing allocator; never mix allocators; arena is not a bound; std.testing.allocator in tests.

security.best_practice: Upstream's position is the same: ReleaseSafe for deployed code, explicit checks that survive ReleaseFast, and suspicion of FFI/process/build-script boundaries; the Zig project also moved development off GitHub to Codeberg in late 2025, which affects where pinned source is fetched from - worth one line in the guide's dependency section.
security.evidence: Release-note and std changes in 0.16 are consistent with the guide; the Codeberg migration is corroborated by the 0.16.0 source tree being hosted there (codeberg.org/ziglang/zig tag 0.16.0) in current references.
security.guide_position: FFI/casts/int-to-pointer/dynamic loading/build scripts/child processes are privileged boundaries; argv-form child processes; ReleaseSafe preferred for safety-sensitive production; reviewed crypto only.

static_analysis.best_practice: Zig still ships no official linter or static analyzer comparable to clang-tidy: the compiler's own diagnostics, safety checks and ZLS diagnostics are the whole official story in 0.16. The gap is therefore the ecosystem's, not a guide error - but the guide never says this, leaving a reader to wonder which tool fills the slot its sibling guides fill with clang-tidy.
static_analysis.evidence: The 0.16.0 documentation/release materials consulted name no analyzer; ZLS (the paired LSP) provides diagnostics only. ziglang.org itself returned HTTP 403 to this audit's fetcher, so this aspect rests on the release-note/doc set rather than an exhaustive site search - hence not-addressed rather than a stronger claim.
static_analysis.guide_position: No analyzer is named: the SKILL pairing is zls + zig fmt + lldb-dap, and assurance rests on compiler diagnostics, runtime safety checks and testing across build modes.

testing.best_practice: zig test with std.testing remains the official route; 0.16 also ships built-in fuzzing support via the test runner/build system, which the guide does not mention - an addition, not a correction.
testing.evidence: The guide's multi-mode test matrix is more rigorous than upstream's baseline advice; the fuzzing gap is recorded as a proposal below.
testing.guide_position: std.testing boundary cases, std.testing.allocator for owned allocations, allocation-failure injection per acquisition step, tests run in Debug, ReleaseSafe and ReleaseFast so rejection survives disabled safety checks.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: 0.16.0 (released 2026-04-13) is still the current stable release: no 0.16.1 exists yet (a Sep 2026 downstream note records a fix 'backported to the 0.16.x branch, but there is no 0.16.1 release yet'), and master is 0.17.0-dev. ZLS tracks the same version line (ZLS 0.16.0, May 2026).
toolchain_pins.evidence: Release date and currency corroborated by the official release-notes URL the guide cites and by current packaging (AUR zig0.16-bin 0.16.0-1, Oct 2026). Note: ziglang.org returned HTTP 403 to this audit's fetcher, so the 'no patch release' point rests on the downstream backport note plus packaging records, not a direct download-index fetch.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Pin Zig 0.16.0 exactly (compiler, target triple, libc, optimisation mode); copy signatures only from that version's stdlib; zls for LSP (unversioned in the guide), zig fmt, lldb-dap.

current_versions.ZLS: 0.16.0 (May 2026), version-matched to Zig 0.16 as upstream intends
current_versions.Zig: 0.16.0, released 2026-04-13 - current stable; no 0.16.1 patch release yet; master is 0.17.0-dev; project development now hosted on Codeberg
current_versions.lldb-dap: Generic LLVM DAP adapter (LLVM 22.1.x); Zig has no language-specific debugger - pairing is a diver-config choice, not an upstream Zig recommendation
current_versions.zig fmt: Built into the 0.16.0 toolchain; canonical formatter

proposals.evidence: The 0.16 toolchain's test/build system includes fuzzing of test inputs; the guide's testing section - otherwise the most complete of the four guides - relies solely on enumerated boundary cases, the exact weakness fuzzing addresses for parsers.
proposals.proposal: Add Zig's built-in fuzzing (zig build test --fuzz / fuzzable test cases) to the testing workflow for byte parsers and decoders, alongside the existing Debug/ReleaseSafe/ReleaseFast matrix.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt for parser-shaped code; keep the enumerated boundary matrix as the deterministic gate and treat fuzzing as a corpus-growing supplement.

proposals.evidence: 0.16 release-note summaries list @cImport deprecation in favour of translate-c (b.addTranslateC()) among the release's breaking/deprecating changes; the guide's language-specific section lists five review boundaries (allocator, borrow, build-mode safety, comptime cost, C ABI) without naming how C headers should now be consumed.
proposals.proposal: Name the 0.16 C-interop route in the FFI/security sections: prefer translate-c via the build system over @cImport, which 0.16 deprecates - otherwise readers will copy pre-0.16 @cImport snippets the guide elsewhere warns against transplanting.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a one-paragraph addition to §18/§26; flag for re-verification against the pinned toolchain because this audit could not fetch ziglang.org directly (HTTP 403).
